title: AI-assisted 2.5D dungeon-crawler engine, WIP. Focused on "create your own gameplay" features. Will be free public release :)
author: Massive-Deer3290

replies.author: Massive-Deer3290
replies.body:
It uses vanilla **WebGL 2** directly. The entire 3D world is rendered using **Raymarching** inside a custom fragment shader.

Instead of traditional 3D meshes and a scene graph (what Three.js handles), this engine calculates the distance to surfaces (Signed Distance Fields or SDFs) for every pixel in real-time. This allows for the highly procedural geometry, smooth blending (blobs), and complex mathematical distortions, without any 3D object imports.

replies.author: Massive-Deer3290
replies.body:
Current phase is pushing the engine and shaders higher, yeah. All the graphics are controlled by complicated math formulae, the GPU is literally doing math in real-time to create the graphics.

So a single digit error in a file can bork the entire rendering.

Hence I've been building a HelpLibrary for users (and the AI) to reference about itself.

comments.author: -RoopeSeta-
comments.body: How long have made this? This cannot be done in a week.

replies.author: Massive-Deer3290
replies.body:
I started it on Jan. 10 so you're right its been more like 9 days.

I have used AI's help with a lot of the coding for the engine. But I set up a project workflow where everything is heavily modulated. It doesn't need to rewrite a shader file with 1000 lines of code, because everything has been turned into subsystems.

It also used pieces of code and raymarching geometry I was playing with while making other apps.

So if this has taken 9 days its because I sat down with a few months of prep and research work ready to go.
